Pain Management (Acute and Chronic Pain Management)

Pain is an unpleasant sensory and emotional experience associated with actual or potential tissue damage. The relationship between pain (subjective) and actual or potential tissue damage (objective) is influenced by socio-cultural context as well as the nervous system.

blocks.text: Multimodal approach; IM/ IV analgesics and/or a central neuraxial or locoregional anaesthetic block may be used. The analgesic effect of these techniques may extend into the early postoperative period. However, it is best to assess pain frequently to determine additional demand of analgesia.

blocks.text: Chronic Non-Cancer Pain: A biopsychosocial assessment is necessary for effective pain management. Look out for the etiology and perpetuating factors and manage accordingly. Note that there may be overlap between different aetiologies, and condition specific pain management is paramount.
